chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Minhāl ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A scorpion is brought out of the well dead. He said, “Draw from it ten buckets.” He said: So I said: And what about other carcasses? He said, “All carcasses are the same, except a carcass that has become putrid. If it is a carcass that has become putrid, then draw from it one hundred buckets; and if the odor still overcomes it after one hundred buckets, then drain it all.”
So the proper way regarding this narration is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation rather than obligation, so that it does not conflict with the earlier reports.

key_terms.أُجِيفَتْ: became putrid or decayed such that odor spreads
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed
key_terms.الْجِيَفِ: animal carcasses or dead bodies found in the water
key_terms.الْعَقْرَبُ: a scorpion found dead in the well
key_terms.فَانْزَحْهَا كُلَّهَا: drain all of the well water completely
key_terms.مِائَةَ دَلْوٍ: one hundred buckets to be drawn from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dead scorpion or other carcass is found in a well?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on a well from which a dead scorpion or other carcass is removed, specifying amounts of water to be drawn depending on the condition of the carcass. The closing statement explains that this report is understood as indicating istihbab (recommendation) rather than obligation, in order to reconcile it with earlier narrations.
